chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not prescribe for women a Qada (make-up) of fasting, nor fasting other than the fasting of Ramadan, except if it is a vow, or expiation fasting, or voluntary fasting.
ai.seo_question: Do women need to make up missed Ramadan fasts?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the juristic consensus that women are exempt from making up missed obligatory fasts of Ramadan due to menstruation or postpartum bleeding, distinguishing this from general voluntary fasts which also do not require makeup unless vowed. This ruling underscores the Shia view of natural physiological states as valid excuses for exemption rather than deficiency, reinforcing the mercy and flexibility in Islamic legislation. The hadith clarifies that while the obligation to fast remains, the mechanism for fulfillment adapts to the specific cause of absence, ensuring no undue burden is placed on women.
